correctness.rationale: For G all simplex stabilizers are pointwise and the ordered-face quotient is a valid cellular chain model. Exact independent algorithms produce G cell counts (1,1,2,1), boundary matrices d2=(1,1) and d3=(-2,2), whose degree-one two-cell contraction yields the order-two Moore space. C11 and C5 orbit matrices give exact Smith factors d2=(1^4,11),d3=(1^4,2) and d1=(1^2),d2=(1^9),d3=(1^10,2), respectively, proving the stated integral homologies. All chain products are zero and original X Smith factors are independently reproduced.

value.rationale: The original tournament has a published nontrivial Moore two-torsion summand and ten free sphere classes, but quotient topology is not determined by its nonequivariant wedge decomposition. The natural affine symmetry collapses the free contribution while retaining precisely the Moore-space homotopy type, and its translation subgroup introduces new eleven-torsion in first quotient homology. The exact group-quotient homotopy classification and integral subgroup torsion profile are mathematically motivated, non-tautological topological invariants of a canonical doubly regular tournament, not a routine recomputation of the known original-space homology.
